claims.text: Stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation can be deliberately introduced into tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys.
The coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
The coherent precipitate interfaces relieve local stress concentrations that could cause premature crack initiation.
Coherent nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature plastic strain and toughness.
The enhancement in plastic strain and toughness occurs by delaying strain localization and crack initiation.
The unperturbed material is a homogeneous single-phase BCC tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloy with little or no coherent nanoprecipitation.
A spark plasma sintering route can serve as SCCP processing to induce the proposed coherent nanoprecipitates.
Carefully designed thermo-mechanical treatment can develop the SCCP microstructure.
The relevant coherent nanoprecipitates form solely within a BCC matrix.
The coherent interfaces are low-energy interfaces.
The precipitate interfaces steadily accommodate large numbers of dislocations during plastic deformation.
Small coherent particles with lattice parameters similar to the matrix reduce elastic interactions with cutting dislocations and help prevent interfacial crack initiation.
Relative to an alloy without tailored precipitate control, the SCCP-treated alloy will have higher uniform elongation at 800–1200 °C.
Relative to the baseline, the SCCP-treated alloy will display a more homogeneous plastic-deformation profile.
Relative to the baseline, the SCCP-treated alloy will show delayed crack initiation during high-temperature loading.
The cited mechanism and ductility benefit apply throughout 800–1200 °C and under tensile, creep, and dynamic loading.
The proposed 800–1200 °C strain-rate-controlled tests mimic fusion-reactor loading conditions.
The magnitude of the mechanical benefit varies with precipitate size, spacing, and volume fraction.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis uses SCCP to mean stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitation, whereas the intervention parenthetically associates SCCP with a spark plasma sintering route. The cited evidence defines SCCP as the precipitation strategy, not spark plasma sintering.

The proposed system is described as a homogeneous BCC matrix with precipitates within that matrix, but the cited demonstrated SCCP alloy contains δ-lamellae and γ″ particles in a BCC+FCC dual-phase matrix.
